Trade Store Adds Space in Two Stages
By Frances Ibarra, Pemberton
Thurlow Trade Supply is enlarging its Pemberton outlet in two stages, with a temporary entrance in use until the work ends.
The store occupies most of a two-level converted warehouse. Bulk orders sit on the upper level, which staff reach by a freight elevator shared with the sign-making workshop that rents the rest of that level; customers wait at the counter while items are carried down. --[1]--.
Construction of the extension is under way and will continue for about two months. The contractor counter and the lumberyard stay open throughout. --[2]--. While the work continues, deliveries and customer pickups both use a temporary gate at the rear of the yard, as the main vehicle entrance is closed. --[3]--.
The first stage, which opens on March 3, adds tool and fastener aisles on the extension's ground floor. Only holders of a Thurlow trade account may enter the new aisles at that stage, and account numbers will be checked at the aisle entrance. A second contractor counter and an indoor paint mixing area will follow in the second stage, from April 14, and the extension is open to every customer from that date. --[4]--.

Time Away From Your Workspace
Members who will be away for several weeks do not have to end their agreement. Loxley Workspace lets you pause billing for a set number of days each membership year. Paid days you do not use are not refunded. Instead, they are added to the end of your current term. The option is open to members whose payments are up to date.
Plan level | Maximum suspended days per membership year* |
Flex Desk | 14 |
Reserved Desk | 30 |
Private Office | 45 |
*Suspended days must be taken in blocks of at least 5 and no more than 20 consecutive days.
How to request a pause
1. Sign in and open the Membership tab, then choose Pause Membership. Your request must be received at least 10 days before your next billing date.
2. Enter the first and last day of your planned absence. The dates you enter must meet the block limits shown above.
3. Submit the request and wait for our written confirmation, which is sent within three business days.
Members who do not use the website may instead ask front desk staff to file a request for them.
Please note: While your membership is suspended, your entry card remains active during staffed reception hours, and letters and parcels are still accepted at the front desk. PROGRAM NEWS
Category Panels Take Over the Awards Judging
By Bernard Tomlin, Members' Bulletin
For several years, every entry to the Alliance Awards was read by the same in-house committee at the association office. That committee now prepares the scoring guide only. Each award category is reviewed instead by a small group of people who put their names forward from member businesses. "A single committee could not read every entry with the care it deserved," said Yvette Bouchard, awards coordinator. "People who run a business judge these entries better than we did."
Every session opens with the chair going through the scoring guide with the panel, before any entry is opened. Entries are then scored one at a time, and each panel agrees on its shortlist before leaving the room.
The placements now posted are provisional. Checking of entries continues to the end of February, and a panel may still be altered where a category gains or loses entries. Volunteers are asked to confirm their attendance with the awards office by February 20.

Late Shopping Evenings Draw Steady Crowds
By Janet Whelan, Local Business
Shops in central Havelock stayed open until 9:00 p.m. on two evenings last week, and the Havelock Retailers' Association reports steady visitor numbers.
"Thursday was busier than any Saturday this year, and most of those who came in had never visited us," said Arnold Deming, who runs a bookstore on Priory Lane.
The blocks did not open late on the evenings first announced. The South Block shops opened late on Wednesday, October 8, and the North Block on Thursday, October 9, the members having agreed to exchange the two dates.
The association, which meets on the last Tuesday of each month, has forty-one members, and thirty-four opened on one of the two evenings. Every participating shop appeared in a flyer delivered across the town, and the cost of printing and delivery was divided among them by storefront width. Officers say a further promotion is planned, but no date is fixed.
